name: ICM-42688-P 6-axis IMU (accelerometer + gyroscope)
description: TDK InvenSense 16-bit 3-axis accelerometer (±2/4/8/16 g) and 3-axis gyroscope (±15.625 to ±2000 °/s) with an I2C/SPI/I3C interface and a die temperature sensor. Sold as: "ICM-42688 6-Axis IMU Accelerometer Gyroscope, I2C SPI Interface" blue 8-pin module (Amazon ASIN B0F3JWY1XF, QUAINTBYTE), about 13 × 13 mm with two 4-pin rows (SDO, SDA, SCL, CS on one edge; INT, FSY, GND, 3V3 on the other), no regulator (3V3 goes straight to the chip, 1.71–3.6 V), I2C pull-ups only when the back solder jumper is closed, I2C address 0x68 with SDO tied to GND (0x69 with SDO to 3.3 V).
eli5: Feels which way is down and how fast it is turning, so your board knows tilt, shakes and spins.

pins.name: SDO
pins.description: Header 1 pin 1. Chip AP_SDO/AP_AD0: I2C address bit. Tied to GND here = 0x68 (tie to 3.3 V instead for 0x69); never leave it floating. SPI data out in SPI mode

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: Header 1 pin 2 (printed SDA/SDI). I2C data (SPI data in). No pull-up unless the back I2C solder jumper is closed, so an external 4.7 kΩ to 3.3 V is added

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: Header 1 pin 3. I2C clock (SPI clock). No pull-up unless the back I2C solder jumper is closed, so an external 4.7 kΩ to 3.3 V is added

pins.name: CS
pins.description: Header 1 pin 4. SPI chip select. The datasheet says to connect it to VDDIO for I2C, so it is tied to 3.3 V here; low selects SPI

pins.name: INT
pins.description: Header 2 pin 1. Interrupt 1 output (open drain by default, active low). Not needed for basic use

pins.name: FSY
pins.description: Header 2 pin 2. Chip pin 9: INT2 output by default (open drain), or FSYNC / CLKIN input. Leave unconnected, or tie to GND if you configure it as FSYNC and do not use it

pins.name: 3V3
pins.description: Header 2 pin 4. Supply straight to the chip's VDD and VDDIO, 1.71–3.6 V (no regulator: never 5 V)

buildNotes: Power from 3V3 only (1.71–3.6 V straight to the chip, absolute max 4 V). There is no regulator: 5 V destroys it.
For I2C, tie CS to 3.3 V (datasheet: connect AP_CS to VDDIO) and tie SDO to GND (0x68) or to 3.3 V (0x69). A floating SDO gives an unpredictable address; CS pulled low switches the chip to SPI.
The board's I2C pull-ups are only connected when the 'I2C' solder jumper on the back is bridged. Either bridge it or fit 4.7 kΩ pull-ups from SDA and SCL to 3.3 V (not both).
WHO_AM_I (0x75) reads 0x47. Soft reset: write 0x01 to DEVICE_CONFIG (0x11) and wait 1 ms.
The chip powers up asleep and reads -32768: write PWR_MGMT0 (0x4E) = 0x0F (gyro + accel low-noise), wait 200 µs before the next write, and about 30 ms (gyro start-up) before using data.
Data is two's complement, high byte first: TEMP 0x1D-0x1E, accel X/Y/Z 0x1F-0x24, gyro X/Y/Z 0x25-0x2A. A 14-byte burst from 0x1D reads everything.

Ranges are coded in reverse of most chips: ACCEL_FS_SEL 0 = ±16 g (2048 LSB/g) ... 3 = ±2 g (16384); GYRO_FS_SEL 0 = ±2000 °/s (16.4 LSB/°/s). The driver uses ±4 g (8192 LSB/g) and ±500 °/s (65.5 LSB/°/s).
Temperature = TEMP_DATA / 132.48 + 25 °C (die temperature, a little above the air).

driver.code:
# ICM-42688-P 6-axis IMU (TDK InvenSense), MicroPython I2C driver.
# Written from the TDK datasheet DS-000347:
#   WHO_AM_I 0x75 = 0x47, REG_BANK_SEL 0x76 (bank 0 holds everything used here)
#   DEVICE_CONFIG 0x11 bit0 = soft reset (wait 1 ms before any other access)
#   PWR_MGMT0 0x4E: GYRO_MODE bits 3:2, ACCEL_MODE bits 1:0 (11 = low-noise mode); the chip powers up asleep
#   GYRO_CONFIG0 0x4F: GYRO_FS_SEL bits 7:5 (000 = +-2000 dps ... 010 = +-500 dps), GYRO_ODR bits 3:0
#   ACCEL_CONFIG0 0x50: ACCEL_FS_SEL bits 7:5 (000 = +-16 g ... 011 = +-2 g), ACCEL_ODR bits 3:0
#   TEMP_DATA 0x1D-0x1E, ACCEL_DATA X/Y/Z 0x1F-0x24, GYRO_DATA X/Y/Z 0x25-0x2A:
#   16-bit two's complement, high byte first (INTF_CONFIG0 SENSOR_DATA_ENDIAN = 1, the default)
#   Temperature degC = TEMP_DATA / 132.48 + 25
# I2C address: 0x68 with AP_AD0 (board pin SDO) low, 0x69 with it high.
# For I2C the chip's CS pin must be held high (tied to VDDIO).
import time

_DEVICE_CONFIG = 0x11
_TEMP_DATA1 = 0x1D
_PWR_MGMT0 = 0x4E
_GYRO_CONFIG0 = 0x4F
_ACCEL_CONFIG0 = 0x50
_WHO_AM_I = 0x75
_REG_BANK_SEL = 0x76

# full scale -> (FS_SEL code, LSB per unit), datasheet sections 3.1, 3.2, 14.37, 14.38
_ACC = {16: (0, 2048.0), 8: (1, 4096.0), 4: (2, 8192.0), 2: (3, 16384.0)}
_GYR = {2000: (0, 16.4), 1000: (1, 32.8), 500: (2, 65.5), 250: (3, 131.0),
        125: (4, 262.0), 62.5: (5, 524.3), 31.25: (6, 1048.6), 15.625: (7, 2097.2)}
_ODR_100HZ = 0x08  # ODR code 1000 = 100 Hz (valid in low-noise mode for both sensors)


def _s16(hi, lo):
    v = (hi << 8) | lo
    return v - 65536 if v & 0x8000 else v


class ICM42688:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=None, accel_range=4, gyro_range=500):
        """addr=None tries 0x68 (SDO to GND) then 0x69 (SDO to 3.3 V)."""
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = None
        for a in ((addr,) if addr is not None else (0x68, 0x69)):
            try:
                if i2c.readfrom_mem(a, _WHO_AM_I, 1)[0] == 0x47:
                    self.addr = a
                    break
            except OSError:
                pass
        if self.addr is None:
            raise OSError('ICM-42688-P not found (WHO_AM_I 0x47 at 0x68/0x69): check wiring, CS high, SDO tied')
        self._w(_REG_BANK_SEL, 0)
        # Soft reset, then wait (datasheet: 1 ms before any other register access).
        try:
            self._w(_DEVICE_CONFIG, 0x01)
        except OSError:
            pass
        time.sleep_ms(2)
        if self._r(_WHO_AM_I, 1)[0] != 0x47:
            raise OSError('ICM-42688-P did not come back after soft reset')
        self._w(_REG_BANK_SEL, 0)
        code, self._acc_lsb = _ACC[accel_range]
        self._w(_ACCEL_CONFIG0, (code << 5) | _ODR_100HZ)
        code, self._gyr_lsb = _GYR[gyro_range]
        self._w(_GYRO_CONFIG0, (code << 5) | _ODR_100HZ)
        # Gyro + accel in low-noise mode, temperature sensor on.
        self._w(_PWR_MGMT0, 0x0F)
        # No register writes for 200 us after leaving OFF; gyro start-up 30 ms, accel 10 ms,
        # plus one 10 ms sample period before the data registers hold a valid sample.
        time.sleep_ms(50)

    def _w(self, reg, val):
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(self.addr, reg, bytes([val]))

    def _r(self, reg, n):
        return self.i2c.readfrom_mem(self.addr, reg, n)

    def read(self):
        """Return ((ax, ay, az) in g, (gx, gy, gz) in deg/s, temperature in degC) from one 14-byte burst."""
        d = self._r(_TEMP_DATA1, 14)
        t = _s16(d[0], d[1]) / 132.48 + 25
        a = tuple(_s16(d[i], d[i + 1]) / self._acc_lsb for i in (2, 4, 6))
        g = tuple(_s16(d[i], d[i + 1]) / self._gyr_lsb for i in (8, 10, 12))
        return a, g, t

    def acceleration(self):
        return self.read()[0]

    def gyro(self):
        return self.read()[1]

    def temperature(self):
        """Die temperature in degC (TEMP_DATA / 132.48 + 25)."""
        d = self._r(_TEMP_DATA1, 2)
        return _s16(d[0], d[1]) / 132.48 + 25

    def sleep(self):
        """Turn accel and gyro off (keep the gyro on at least 45 ms before this)."""
        self._w(_PWR_MGMT0, 0x00)

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from icm42688 import ICM42688

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}), freq=400000)
imu = ICM42688(i2c)  # 0x68 (SDO to GND) or 0x69; +-4 g, +-500 dps
while True:
    (ax, ay, az), (gx, gy, gz), t = imu.read()
    print('A=%.2f,%.2f,%.2fg G=%.1f,%.1f,%.1fdps T=%.1fC' % (ax, ay, az, gx, gy, gz, t))
    time.sleep(1)
